rewrites.summary:
This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. A trans visitor stands under the national framework documented in the sources: same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned with no specific legal protections; the 'gay propaganda' law carries administrative fines with repeat offences punishable by up to 4 years in prison, and the extremism designation of the LGBT movement carries 2-6 years for participating and 6-10 for organising.

Enforcement of the framework is active and documented: between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 people were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws (convictions, detentions, extremism prosecutions); courts have issued 101 convictions tied to the extremism designation following the 2023 national court ruling, with participants facing up to 12 years in prison. For a trans visitor, visible LGBT status carries concrete arrest, prosecution and detention risk in practice despite the absence of a general ban on same-sex activity. The source note contains no division-specific findings, so the assessment rests on the national baseline, with a local divergence claimed in neither direction.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Scoring and national context: the division sits at the national score because the dossier identified no material deviation (±0.02), and the sources record no division-level court action, national-policy change or difference in application distinguishing this division; the framework that drives the visitor assessment applies uniformly, so no adjacent circumstance modifies it for this division.
rewrites.localsOnly: The 2023 legal-gender-recognition and gender-affirming-care bans are resident-facing; the extremism-designation machinery (convictions, NGO liquidation) targets resident organisations and individuals. No division-level resident data — cultural-role, birth-register or resident-discrimination statistics — are recorded in the sources for this division.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
Advisory-level risks are trans-unrelated: the ongoing war, wrongful-detention risk, and arbitrary law enforcement affect any traveller regardless of LGBT status.

No source in the dossier addresses border screening, documents or passport-marker practice for trans visitors to this division, and no division-specific divergence from the national framework is documented in either direction.
